simple.meaning: בַּקְבּוּק (Baqbûwq) is a Hebrew word meaning “Bakbuk , one of the Nethinim.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: בַּקְבּוּק (H1227) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Ezra 2:51, with occurrences in Ezra, Nehemiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בַּקְבּוּק (H1227) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in בַּקְבּוּק (H1227) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: בַּקְבּוּק (Baqbûwq) / H1227 is traced through Ezra 2:51, Nehemiah 7:53 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H1227. Baqbuq בַּקְבּוּק proper name, masculine head of a family of Nethinim ; ׳בניבֿ Ezra 2:51 ; Neh 7:53 .
